claim: R4 is version 4.0.1, a "Mixed Normative and STU" release, and HL7's R4 pages say "The current version which supercedes this version is 5.0.0".
quote: This page is part of the FHIR Specification (v4.0.1: R4 - Mixed Normative and STU ) in it's permanent home (it will always be available at this URL). The current version which supercedes this version is 5.0.0 .

claim: The Vital Signs profile page carries the same version notice.
quote: The current version which supercedes this version is 5.0.0

claim: HL7 defines Observation as "Measurements and simple assertions made about a patient, device or other subject."
quote: Measurements and simple assertions made about a patient, device or other subject.

claim: Its listed uses include "Vital signs such as body weight, blood pressure, and temperature"...
quote: Vital signs such as body weight , blood pressure , and temperature

claim: ...and "Device measurements such as EKG data or Pulse Oximetry data".
quote: Device measurements such as EKG data or Pulse Oximetry data

claim: The Vital Signs profile: a single vocabulary is needed "Particularly with the use of wearables by patients where they want to/need to share information from those devices."
quote: Vital signs will be one of the first areas where there is a need for a single, global vocabulary to allow for ubiquitous access and re-use. Particularly with the use of wearables by patients where they want to/need to share information from those devices.

claim: In R4 the Observation resource is "Normative (from v4.0.0)".
quote: Normative (from v4.0.0)

claim: The Vital Signs profile page gives its standards status as Informative.
quote: Standards Status : Informative

claim: "At its simplest, a resource instance can consist of only a code and a value, and status flag."
quote: At its simplest, a resource instance can consist of only a code and a value, and status flag.

claim: status is 1..1: registered, preliminary, final, amended and further codes, from a required code list.
quote: status | ?! Σ | 1..1 | code | registered | preliminary | final | amended + ObservationStatus ( Required )

claim: code is 1..1, with LOINC as the example binding.
quote: code | Σ | 1..1 | CodeableConcept | Type of observation (code / type) LOINC Codes ( Example )

claim: subject is 0..1: a Patient, Group, Device or Location.
quote: subject | Σ | 0..1 | Reference ( Patient | Group | Device | Location ) | Who and/or what the observation is about

claim: effective[x] is 0..1: the clinically relevant time or period, as a dateTime, Period, Timing or instant.
quote: effective[x] | Σ | 0..1 | | Clinically relevant time/time-period for observation | effectiveDateTime | | | dateTime | | effectivePeriod | | | Period | | effectiveTiming | | | Timing | | effectiveInstant | | | instant

claim: issued is 0..1: when this version was made available.
quote: issued | Σ | 0..1 | instant | Date/Time this version was made available

claim: value[x] is 0..1, as a Quantity, CodeableConcept, string, boolean, integer, Range, Ratio, SampledData, time, dateTime or Period.
quote: Observation.value[x] : 0..1 Actual result . One of these 11

claim: The eleven value types.
quote: valueQuantity valueCodeableConcept valueString valueBoolean valueInteger valueRange valueRatio valueSampledData valueTime valueDateTime valuePeriod

claim: dataAbsentReason is 0..1: why the result is missing.
quote: dataAbsentReason | I | 0..1 | CodeableConcept | Why the result is missing

claim: device is 0..1: the measuring Device or DeviceMetric.
quote: device | | 0..1 | Reference ( Device | DeviceMetric ) | (Measurement) Device

claim: component is 0..*: results read together, such as systolic and diastolic pressure.
quote: Observations that are commonly produced and interpreted together. For example, systolic and diastolic blood pressure are represented as a single Blood pressure panel .

claim: derivedFrom and hasMember link the observations a value was made from, or the members a panel groups.
quote: hasMember | Σ | 0..* | Reference ( Observation | QuestionnaireResponse | MolecularSequence ) | Related resource that belongs to the Observation group

claim: derivedFrom: related measurements the observation is made from.
quote: Related measurements the observation is made from

claim: Rule obs-6 says "dataAbsentReason SHALL only be present if Observation.value[x] is not present".
quote: obs-6 | Rule | (base) | dataAbsentReason SHALL only be present if Observation.value[x] is not present

claim: Rule obs-7: if Observation.code matches a component's code, the value for that code "SHALL NOT be present".
quote: obs-7 | Rule | (base) | If Observation.code is the same as an Observation.component.code then the value element associated with the code SHALL NOT be present

claim: effectiveDateTime or effectivePeriod "is the time that the observation is most relevant as an observation of the subject", which for a person is "the physiologically relevant time of the observation".
quote: The effectiveDateTime or effectivePeriod is the time that the observation is most relevant as an observation of the subject. For a biological subject (e.g. a human patient), this is the physiologically relevant time of the observation.

claim: For an observation obtained directly from the subject, such as blood pressure, it is the start and end of the observation process.
quote: In the case of an observation obtained directly from a subject (e.g. BP, Chest X-ray), this is the start and end time of the observation process

claim: The Observation page says that if implementations use the resource to express the profile's concepts as structured data, "they SHALL conform to the following profiles", naming Vital signs.
quote: If implementations use this Resource when expressing the profile-specific concepts as structured data, they SHALL conform to the following profiles:

claim: "When a FHIR implementation supports any of the vital signs listed below, the implementation SHALL conform to this profile for the vital sign observation."
quote: When a FHIR implementation supports any of the vital signs listed below, the implementation SHALL conform to this profile for the vital sign observation.

claim: Each vital-signs Observation must have a status...
quote: The following data-elements are mandatory (i.e. data SHALL be present).

claim: ...a category code of 'vital-signs'...
quote: a category code of 'vital-signs'

claim: ...a LOINC code for what is measured, which the profile calls the "magic value"...
quote: a "magic value" which tells you what is being measured

claim: ...LOINC was chosen for the magic values.
quote: LOINC was chosen for the "magic values" because this aligns with the most countries

claim: ...a time indicating when the measurement was taken...
quote: a time indicating when the measurement was taken

claim: ...a numeric result value with a standard UCUM unit...
quote: a numeric result value and standard UCUM unit which is taken from the Unit Code column in the table below.

claim: ...or, when there is no numeric result, a reason.
quote: note: if there is no numeric result then you have to supply a reason

claim: Vital signs panel 85353-1, with member observations linked with hasMember and no value.
quote: When used, Observation.valueQuantity is not present; instead, related links (with type=has-member) reference the vital signs observations

claim: Vital signs panel code 85353-1.
quote: Vital Signs Panel 85353-1

claim: Respiratory rate 9279-1, /min.
quote: Respiratory Rate 9279-1 Respiratory Rate /min

claim: Heart rate 8867-4, /min.
quote: Heart rate 8867-4 Heart rate - To supplement this vital sign observation, 8887-2 - Heart rate device type MAY be included as an additional observation. /min

claim: Oxygen saturation 2708-6, %.
quote: Oxygen saturation 2708-6 Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood

claim: Oxygen saturation unit %.
quote: 59408-5 Oxygen saturation in Arterial blood by Pulse oximetry which MAY be included as an additional observation code. % Oxygen Saturation Example

claim: Body temperature 8310-5, Cel or [degF].
quote: MAY be used as additional observations. Cel, [degF] Body Temperature Example

claim: Body temperature code 8310-5.
quote: Body temperature 8310-5 Body temperature

claim: Body height 8302-2, cm or [in_i].
quote: Body height 8302-2 Body height

claim: Body height unit cm or [in_i].
quote: MAY be included as an additional observation code. cm, [in_i] Body height Example

claim: Head circumference 9843-4, cm or [in_i].
quote: Head circumference 9843-4 Head Occipital-frontal circumference cm, [in_i]

claim: Body weight 29463-7, g, kg or [lb_av].
quote: Body weight 29463-7 Body weight

claim: Body weight unit g, kg or [lb_av].
quote: g, kg,[lb_av] Body Weight Example

claim: Body mass index 39156-5, kg/m2.
quote: Body mass index 39156-5 Body mass index (BMI) [Ratio] kg/m2

claim: Blood pressure panel 85354-9, no value; systolic and diastolic go in components.
quote: Blood pressure panel with all children optional - This is a component observation. It has no value in Observation.valueQuantity and contains at least one component (systolic and/or diastolic).

claim: Blood pressure panel code 85354-9.
quote: Blood pressure systolic and diastolic 85354-9

claim: Systolic blood pressure 8480-6, mm[Hg].
quote: Systolic blood pressure 8480-6 Systolic blood pressure - Observation.component code for a blood pressure Observation mm[Hg]

claim: Diastolic blood pressure 8462-4, mm[Hg].
quote: Diastolic blood pressure 8462-4 Diastolic blood pressure - Observation.component code for a blood pressure Observation mm[Hg]

claim: For blood pressure, "you must have both a systolic and a diastolic component, though one or both may have dataAbsentReason instead of a value."
quote: In addition, if you have a blood pressure observation, you must have both a systolic and a diastolic component, though one or both may have dataAbsentReason instead of a value.

claim: The bindings are extensible.
quote: These are extensible bindings and require that when a system supports any of these vital signs concepts, they must represent them using these codes.

claim: If you also record a more specific code, "implementers must support both the values (LOINC) listed below and the translated code".
quote: If a more specific code or another code system is recorded or required, implementers must support both the values (LOINC) listed below and the translated code

claim: "The table above is the minimum set, additional vital signs are allowed."
quote: The table above is the minimum set, additional vital signs are allowed.

claim: The profile's quick start lists searches servers must support: a patient's vital signs by category, by category and date, and by one or more of the LOINC codes, for example GET [base]/Observation?patient=[id]&category=vital-signs.
quote: A server is capable of returning all of a patient's vital signs that it supports using GET [base]/Observation?patient=[id]&category=vital-signs .

claim: ...by category and date...
quote: Support: Mandatory to support search by category code and date

claim: ...and by one or more of the LOINC codes.
quote: Support: Mandatory to support search by vital sign LOINC(s) listed above.

claim: The code parameter "searches only Observation.code", so searching for the systolic or diastolic component code "will not return the resource", and the profile points to the combo-code search parameter to search both.
quote: The "code" parameter searches only Observation.code . For example when fetching blood pressures the resource will be only be returned when the search is based on 85354-9(Systolic and Diastolic BP). Using the component codes 8480-6(Systolic BP) or 8462-4 (Diastolic BP) will not return the resource . In order to search both Observation.code and Observation.component.code in a single query, use the "combo-code" search parameter.

claim: The profile has the server ensure "that every API request includes a valid Authorization token"...
quote: A server has ensured that every API request includes a valid Authorization token

claim: ...and reject unauthorized requests "by returning an HTTP 401 Unauthorized response code".
quote: A server has rejected any unauthorized requests by returning an HTTP 401 Unauthorized response code.

claim: A waveform, such as ECG samples, goes in valueSampledData.
quote: The special values "E" (error), "L" (below detection limit) and "U" (above detection limit) can be used are in the SampledData data type.

claim: A metric computed from other readings uses derivedFrom, pointing at the source observations.
quote: When linking to other Observations from which an Observation is derived. In this case both Observation.code and Observation.value[x] are present, and the linked observations are listed in Observation.derivedFrom .

claim: HL7's examples use "http://loinc.org" as the coding system for LOINC codes.
quote: "system": "http://loinc.org", "code": "74076-1"

claim: HL7's examples give a valueQuantity with value, unit, system "http://unitsofmeasure.org" and code.
quote: "unit": "mmol/l", "system": "http://unitsofmeasure.org", "code": "mmol/L"

claim: HL7's grouping notes add that "Profiling will normally be necessary for implementation."
quote: Profiling will normally be necessary for implementation.

claim: HL7 also publishes a Personal Health Device FHIR implementation guide, version 2.0.0 (STU 2), based on R4.
quote: This page is part of the Personal Health Device FHIR IG (v2.0.0: STU 2) based on FHIR

claim: HL7 says a body mass index Observation "should not contain components for height and weight because they are clinically relevant observations on their own".
quote: For example a Body Mass Index (BMI) Observation should not contain components for height and weight because they are clinically relevant observations on their own and should be represented by separate Observation resources.

claim: ...and asks for separate Observations linked with derivedFrom instead.
quote: An example of this would be a Body Mass Index (BMI) Observation where the height and weight measurements are referenced.

claim: The FTC's health-app tool says a developer operating an app on behalf of a HIPAA covered entity likely is a business associate.
quote: Are you developing, offering, or operating an app on behalf of a HIPAA covered entity (such as a hospital, doctor’s office, health insurer, or health plan’s wellness program)?

claim: The profile adds that 8887-2, heart rate device type, may be included as an additional observation.
quote: 8887-2 - Heart rate device type MAY be included as an additional observation.

claim: When the reading failed with an error, HL7's Observation notes say to use dataAbsentReason with the value error or NaN.
quote: In addition, when there is an error the dataAbsentReason element should be used with the appropriate value ('error' or 'NaN').
